## Standards

No concrete documented-standard violations were found in `6e76efa93588844996611b86320de7747cca3d24...261bea829e56f9f7fe8e368d31d599e217422290`. No new in-scope baseline smells were identified; the three previously adjudicated smell observations were not repeated.

## Spec

- **High — non-Bearer/Basic Authorization headers can retain the credential value.** Issue authority requires detection of “authorization headers” and replacement of their values with non-reversible placeholders (`.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/materials.md:35-37`); Plan-002 §2 requires that no secret reach staging or the final core. In `src/recorder/scanner.ts:29-36`, the generic authorization alternative consumes only the first whitespace-delimited token. Consequently:

  ```ts
  scanString("Authorization: Token plainsecrettokenvalue999", "probe").value
  // "[REDACTED] plainsecrettokenvalue999"
  ```

  `src/recorder/admit.ts:279-290` stores those partially scanned bytes. The Spec sibling confirmed this end-to-end with a temporary external-authority input: Recorder succeeded and promoted the credential suffix into `inputs/authority`. The scratch probe was deleted; the regex and storage behavior are fixed-target facts.

No other concrete violations were found. The review also rechecked the escape-aware/unmatched and simple quoted-assignment repairs, canonical archive identity fail-closed, exact side-branch references, Git-reference identity, CI/docs repairs, Receipt derivative/audit law, manifest/admission, atomic one-tree publication, host-native lifecycle, reconstruction/no generic payload, exact spawn/outcome/streams, and role isolation. No session payload was inspected.

Summary: Standards — 0 findings. Spec — 1 finding; worst is incomplete Authorization-header redaction allowing credential bytes into the promoted docket.
